activities.anchor: you would rather become someone who does not
activities.caption: pair each wallet answer with its framework
activities.name: ethWalletMatch

config.prompt: Three serious answers to the wallet — pair each with its framework:

pairs.left: return it — a city where wallets come back is one you want to live in
return it — keeping it treats the owner as a means to your convenience
pairs.right: deontology: the duty holds regardless of outcome

pairs.left: ask what an honest person would do
pairs.right: virtue ethics: what kind of person you are becoming

config.why: They are not three recipes producing the same dinners — in hard cases they genuinely disagree.

activities.anchor: The question sounds abstract until you meet its rivals
activities.caption: find the faulty line — normative ethics and its rivals
activities.name: ethNormSpot

config.prompt: One line of this gloss on normative ethics is wrong — click it:
lines: Normative ethics asks what justifies a moral judgement — one that would stand wherever you were raised.
If rightness is whatever the individual thinks, two people who disagree are both correct.
That view explains moral disagreement perfectly, disagreement and all.
If rightness is whatever society approves, every reformer is wrong by definition.
Philosophers look for principles that can be argued for — reasons that survive being questioned.
config.correction: It explains disagreement away, not it: on that view disagreement becomes impossible in principle — yet it is the thing you have whenever you argue with anyone about anything.
config.why: Neither rival can say what the reformer or the dissident is doing right — which is why the search is for principles that survive questioning.

activities.anchor: Bentham, true to his reforming temperament, made the test mechanical
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the felicific calculus
activities.name: ethCalcCloze

config.text: Bentham's calculus scores a pleasure along dimensions: %%0%% (how keen), %%1%% (how long), certainty, %%2%% (how soon), fecundity (will it breed further pleasures?), purity (will it cost pains later?) and %%3%% (how many people?).

activities.anchor: a city must choose between a park or a car park on one plot
activities.caption: bet on which dimensions win
activities.name: ethParkPredict

config.q: The car park pleases 4,000 commuters intensely and certainly; the park pleases 40,000 residents weakly over decades. On which dimensions does the park win?
config.why: Walks become habits, habits improve health, health compounds — the calculus exposes why we hesitate: extent and duration versus intensity and certainty.

activities.anchor: pleasures differ in kind, not just amount
activities.caption: drag the divider — what Mill added
activities.name: ethMillCompare

config.prompt: Drag the divider — what Mill added:

before.label: Bentham: quantity
before.text: Push-pin is as good as poetry if the pleasure is equal — the doctrine of swine; and it cannot explain why an intelligent person's misery can outrank a contented fool's happiness.

after.label: Mill: quality
after.text: Pleasures exercising intellect, imagination and moral feeling are intrinsically superior — tested democratically: those who have experienced both prefer the higher even at the cost of contentment.

config.why: Better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied.

config.root: You are a rule utilitarian. This once, breaking the rule would pay.

choices.label: Break it — utility rules
choices.feedback: Then rules can always be overridden when utility demands — and the view collapses into act utilitarianism.

choices.label: Follow it — the rule binds
choices.feedback: Then the critics' other horn: why not justify the rules directly?

collapse.text: Horn one: override whenever utility demands and rule utilitarianism is act utilitarianism with extra steps.

direct.text: Horn two: never override, and the rules float free of the theory that was meant to ground them.

config.why: Rule utilitarianism trades a little optimisation for stability and trust — and has to say exactly when rules may be overridden.

activities.anchor: binding only on those who share the goal
activities.caption: file each command — hypothetical or categorical
activities.name: ethImperativeSort

items.label: "if you want to be healthy, exercise"
applies only to agents who share the goal
binding unconditionally — what reason itself requires of any rational agent
what the good will acts from, out of respect for the moral law

config.why: The shopkeeper who is honest because honesty pays acts correctly but not morally — moral worth lies in the motive, not the outcome.

activities.anchor: the good of anything that has a function lies in performing that function well
activities.caption: rebuild the function argument
activities.name: ethFunctionOrder

items: A thing's good lies in performing its function well
What is distinctively human is not growth (plants) or perception (animals)
It is activity of the soul in accordance with reason
Therefore human good is rational activity, excellently performed, over a whole life
config.why: Eudaimonia is the final end — the one thing pursued for its own sake; money, honour and pleasure are all pursued for something else.
